newsitem.title: USA: Boeing sends team to Peru to help in crash probe.
newsitem.headline: Boeing sends team to Peru to help in crash probe.

text.p: Boeing Co. is sending an investigator and pilot to help Peruvian authorities determine why a 757-200 airliner crashed into the Pacific Ocean north of Lima on Wednesday, a spokeswoman for the manufacturer said.
All 70 people aboard the Aeroperu twin-engine jet were feared dead.

Boeing spokeswoman Susan Bradley said officials of engine maker Pratt & Whitney, the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board were also heading to the crash site to assist Peruvian investigators.
Bradley said the Aeroperu jet originally had been delivered to a leasing company in December 1992 and had completed 2,630 cycles of service, with each cycle consisting of one takeoff and landing.

The crash was the third involving a 757, which had a perfect safety record from the time it entered commercial service in 1983 until last year, when an American Airlines jet slammed into a mountain in Colombia, killing 159 people.

That crash was blamed on pilot error, but the NTSB Tuesday recommended 17 changes that could help prevent a similar disaster, including improved flight display units and a better ground proximity warning system.

In February, an Alas Nacionales 757-200 operated by Turkish carrier Birgenair crashed into the Caribbean after taking off from the Dominican Republic, killing all 189 people aboard. That crash has also been attributed to pilot error.
